messages:
kevin: Quick brain-dump — I sketched a different approach for canary/A-B rollouts + automated fallback. Calling it 'traffic manifold' for now. Short tl;dr: separate decision plane from routing plane; probes drive a weighted manifold that maps traffic to variants and fallbacks. Thoughts?

jess: curious — how is this different from our current probe -> policy -> splitter flow?

kevin: current flow mixes state in the router and in the policy engine. Idea: keep router dumb (only applies weights), let a compact 'manifold service' own the assignment math and TTLs. Router subscribes to manifold updates.

sam: sounds like pushing complexity into a central service — single source of truth. Is that a performance bottleneck?

kevin: good call. design note: manifold emits precomputed shard -> variant weight tables (epoched). Router fetches deltas, applies them atomically. We keep per-region instances and use signed epochs to avoid split-brain.

olga: How do rollbacks/fallbacks happen? automatic? manual? hybrid?

kevin: hybrid. Probes feed signals (latency, error rate, quality regression score). A decision rule evaluates signals over sliding windows. If threshold hit, manifold shifts weight to fallback variant or reduces weight by X%. Rollback can be automatic if metrics recover, else alert and hold for manual jump.

lin: can we express policies as plain JSON? e.g. a policy block: ```json
{
  "policy_id": "latency-surge-1",
  "signals": ["p95_latency","server_errors"],
  "window_sec": 60,
  "actions": [ { "type":"shift_weight","delta_pct": -30, "to":"baseline" }, { "type":"alert","team":"oncall" } ]
}
```

kevin: yes, intent is policy DSL that's easy to reason about. DSL eval runs in manifold with a sandbox. Actions include shift_weight, route_cutover (drain+flip), throttle, and temporary-allow-list.

sam: what about stateful sessions / affinity? If we change weights mid-flight we can break KV caches and session affinity.

kevin: router will provide a per-request hint header for affinity check: x-manifold-epoch and x-manifold-variant. If affinity present for session, router uses a sticky override unless policy marks session as eligible for rebalance (e.g., new deployment). Also we aim for per-variant warmup so caches persist.

jess: fallback safety — do we have a canary escrow slot to hold a small fraction of traffic in case the fallback itself has an issue?

kevin: yep: manifold supports a reserve 'escrow' bucket. The decision engine can move traffic into escrow instead of immediate baseline fallback, run validation probes against escrow, then promote. That helps avoid double-fallback loops.

olga: telemetry + audit? we need immutable change events for compliance and debugging.

kevin: every manifold epoch is written to the change log with diffs + decision triggers (probe snapshots). We also expose a timeline view in Console and an API for replay. Signed epochs + SHA ensure integrity.

lin: edge-case: if manifold loses connectivity, router should fail open or closed?

sam: depends on SLA. For low-latency read paths we probably fail to last-known-epoch (cached weights). For critical privacy-regulated customers, fail closed to baseline reserved capacity.

jess: ops playbook? quick steps please.

kevin: ops playbook (draft):
1) detect anomaly -> manifold reduces traffic % to escrow and alerts.
2) oncall inspects probe snapshots + logs. If auto-heal triggers, manifold promotes when quality metrics pass for N windows.
3) if not resolved within T minutes, manual rollback to baseline or scale dedicated pool.
4) escalate to infra if manifolds are unhealthy (failover to regional replica).

olga: implementation notes: we should separate decision engine from policy authoring UI so SREs can reuse community policies. Also consider a policy simulator for pre-flight tests.

kevin: agreed. simulator + unit tests + canary policy library (example policies for throughput, latency, regressions).

deploy-bot: [deploy] manifold-service v0.1 deployed to staging at 2026-03-18T02:13:10Z :rocket:

lin: next steps: I'll prototype the epoch format and delta stream (gRPC with compressed protos). Sam — can you run a perf analysis on router delta apply path? Jess — can you sketch Console timeline UI that shows epoch diffs + probe markers?

sam: on it. I'll mock 1k updates/s and measure apply latency + memory.

jess: will do. Mockups by EOD Friday.

kevin: thanks. If folks agree, I'll write a follow-up RFC with diagrams, epoch spec, and policy DSL examples.

olga: +1. Please include regression windows and default thresholds for our supported models.

kevin: noted. I'll add defaults and per-customer override rules.

sam: tiny comment — call it 'manifold' or 'traffic manifold'? branding matters for docs. Maybe 'manifold controller'.

kevin: 'manifold controller' sounds good. I'll use that in the RFC.

lin: wrapping up — saved the sketch in #eng-platform-drive: https://drive.internal/redwood/manifold/outline_v1.pdf :point_up:
